question.text: `Hariyali Foundation`, a forest-conservation NPO in Odisha, receives a EUR 2 lakh grant from a German CSR donor. Under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act 2010 (FCRA), the first receipt of this foreign contribution must land in:

answer.text: Any scheduled commercial bank branch designated by the NPO's Board
The Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai
Any FCRA-registered sub-account at an Authorised Dealer Category-I branch
The State Bank of India, New Delhi Main Branch (FCRA Account)

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 17 of FCRA 2010 (as amended in 2020) mandates that foreign contribution be received only in the 'FCRA Account' opened at the State Bank of India, New Delhi Main Branch (11 Sansad Marg). Subsequent utilisation accounts can be at other scheduled banks, but first receipt is exclusive to SBI NDMB. The Trap: Any scheduled bank was the pre-2020 position — now obsolete. RBI is not the receiver of foreign contribution (it regulates FEMA / ECB). AD Cat-I is a FEMA concept, not FCRA receipt. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV / IFSCA-01 (AML) covers FCRA overlap for AML reporting; XXIII tests the bank-account mechanics specifically. The SBI NDMB rule is SE-side compliance. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Include an SBI NDMB bank statement walkthrough in your FCRA sub-section of the AIR. Any direct credit at a non-SBI account is an FCRA violation of the most serious kind and can trigger cancellation — always confirm the first-hop bank is SBI NDMB before signing off.
